To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the content of immunoreactive ANP in arterial hypertension is determined by its etiological factors; 2) the concentration of the hormone in the blood of patients with arterial hypertension of endocrinogenic genesis is determined by the type and severity of the disease.

the plasma content of immunoreactive ANP in arterial hypertension of endocrinal origin is differentially directed and is dependent on the nature of the underlying pathology and the stage of the disease.
the concentration of immunoreactive ANP is significantly higher in primary aldosteronism and pheochromocytoma and lower in Cushing's disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of atrial natriuetic hormone in the development of arterial hypertension of the endocrine origin.
the role of atrial natriuetic peptide in the regulation of the arterial pressure and water-sal metabolism in patients with various types of arterial hypertension of the endocrine origin.
the role of atrial natriu-retic peptide in the regulation of the water-salt balance and blood pressure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of atrial natriuresis in the pathogenesis is not yet clear.
the role of atrial natriuresis in arterial hypertension of endocrinal genesis is not fully clear.
atrial natriuetic peptide plays a part in the regulation of the arterial pressure and water-salts metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasma concentration of immunoreactive ANP is a marker of the activity of the renin-angiotensin system, which can be used in the differential diagnosis of various types of arterial hypertension.
the plasma content of immunoreactive natriuretic atrial peptide in arterial hypertension of endogenous origin is not a constant value, being subject to considerable fluctuations.
atrial natriaturetic peptide is an important factor in the regulation of the arterial blood pressure and the water-salt balance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
atrial natriu- retic peptide may be used in clinical practice as an additional diagnostic parameter for the evaluation of arterial hypertension of certain endocrine genesis.
the concentration of immunoreactive ANP is a reliable marker for the diagnosis of arterial hypertension of various endocrine origins.
